candidates.next_evidence: Track Walmart U.S. grocery comps, Sam's Club traffic and membership income, private-brand penetration, retail media growth, shrink, gross margin, and whether Great Value/Member's Mark gains are incremental or mainly mix-shifting from national brands.
candidates.node_relation: Direct value-retail and club exposure through Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club; private-label exposure through Great Value, Member's Mark, Marketside, Mainstays and related store brands.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Mass merchant, warehouse club, grocery, retail media
candidates.theme_relation: Large-scale beneficiary of value-seeking consumer behavior, grocery/staples resilience, private-label substitution, retail media/data monetization, and membership income at Sam's Club.
candidates.why_include: Walmart has the purchasing scale, store density, grocery traffic, omnichannel reach, and private-brand platform that fit the node's chokepoint hypothesis. Its April 2026 Great Value redesign across nearly 10,000 food and consumables items is direct evidence that Walmart is investing behind private-label staples while shoppers remain price-sensitive.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify latest comparable club sales excluding gasoline, traffic versus ticket, renewal and higher-tier membership penetration, Own Brands penetration path toward management targets, merchandise gross margin, new-club productivity, and geographic expansion execution.
candidates.node_relation: Pure-play public warehouse club with Own Brands penetration, membership fee income, fuel, grocery/perishables, and regional club expansion.
candidates.theme_relation: Direct exposure to bulk-value purchasing, trade-down into clubs, private-label margin expansion, and recurring membership economics.
candidates.why_include: BJ is less obvious than Costco or Walmart but maps cleanly to the warehouse-club/private-label node. Fiscal 2025 reporting showed Own Brands penetration around 23% of merchandise sales and membership fee income growth, making it a focused way to study whether club-format economics are gaining share in a pressured consumer environment.

candidates.next_evidence: Track comparable sales by banner, merchandise margin, inventory per store, quality of available branded supply, buying-office expansion, shrink, freight, tariff exposure, and whether full-price retail discipline reduces closeout availability.
candidates.node_relation: Largest off-price apparel/home retailer; converts vendor overstocks, cancelled orders, brand inventory imbalances, and consumer value-seeking into traffic and margin opportunities.
candidates.theme_relation: Direct beneficiary of discretionary weakness when brands and full-price retailers create excess inventory, and when consumers trade down but still want branded goods.
candidates.why_include: TJX is an obvious off-price leader but still important for the chokepoint map because the buying organization, vendor relationships, lean inventory model, and treasure-hunt format are difficult to replicate at scale. Its FY2026 10-K explicitly frames opportunistic buying, lean inventory, and frequent inventory turns as key elements of the model.

candidates.next_evidence: Track comparable-store sales, new-store productivity, inventory growth versus sales, gross margin, availability and quality of closeout deals, former Big Lots location conversion, private-label mix, and whether closeout supply tightens if upstream retailers normalize inventories.
candidates.node_relation: Closeout/value retailer sourcing excess inventory and directly sourced private-label products across household goods and consumer categories.
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order beneficiary of retail disruption, manufacturer overproduction, bankruptcies/store closures, and consumers seeking extreme value in discretionary and household categories.
candidates.why_include: Ollie's is a less obvious chokepoint candidate because its edge is not just low prices but access to fragmented closeout supply. Its FY2025 annual report describes a flexible buying model focused on closeout merchandise and excess inventory, augmented by directly sourced private-label products.

candidates.next_evidence: Check customer concentration, Whole Foods/Amazon dependency, private-label/owned-brand sales disclosure, fill rates, distribution-center productivity, margin recovery, leverage, cybersecurity remediation costs, and whether independent grocers are gaining or losing share versus scaled value retailers.
candidates.node_relation: Second-order grocery infrastructure supplier; distributes natural, organic, specialty, produce and conventional groceries and offers own private-label lines to retail customers.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Grocery wholesale distribution and private-label support services
candidates.theme_relation: Indirect exposure to value/private-label staples through independent grocers, natural/specialty retailers, wholesale logistics, owned brands, and retailer support services.
candidates.why_include: UNFI is not a consumer-facing value retailer, but it may be an underappreciated supplier chokepoint if smaller grocers need scale distribution, owned brands, and merchandising support to compete with Walmart, clubs, Aldi, and dollar/value channels. Its fiscal 2025 annual report states that it offers wholesale customers private-label product lines and operates large-scale distribution infrastructure.

evidence.claim: Walmart announced a comprehensive redesign of Great Value, its flagship private brand, spanning almost 10,000 food and consumables items.
evidence.source_title: Walmart Unveils Modern Redesign of Great Value, Its Flagship Private Brand

evidence.claim: Walmart's FY2026 annual report disclosed Sam's Club U.S. net sales of $93.0 billion and described membership income as a significant component of the segment's operating income.

BJ's fiscal 2025 10-K summary reported total revenues of $20.5 billion, comparable club sales growth excluding gasoline of 5.2%, membership fee income growth of 8.5%, and Own Brands penetration of 23%.

evidence.claim: TJX's FY2026 Form 10-K identifies opportunistic buying, relatively lean inventory levels, frequent inventory turns, and the treasure-hunt experience as key elements of its off-price strategy.
evidence.source_title: The TJX Companies, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 31, 2026

evidence.claim: Ollie's FY2025 annual report describes the company as a leading off-price retailer of brand-name household products using a flexible buying model focused on closeout merchandise and excess inventory, supplemented by directly sourced private-label products.
evidence.source_title: Ollie's Bargain Outlet Holdings, Inc. Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report

evidence.claim: UNFI's fiscal 2025 Form 10-K describes the company as a leading distributor of natural, organic, specialty, produce and conventional grocery and non-food products, and says it offers wholesale customers its own private-label product lines.
evidence.source_title: United Natural Foods, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended August 2, 2025

evidence.claim: TreeHouse Foods was a strong private-label manufacturer mapping candidate, but Investindustrial completed its acquisition on February 11, 2026, making it no longer a current US-listed candidate for this universe pass.
evidence.source_title: Investindustrial Completes Acquisition of TreeHouse Foods

memory_update.text: Add WMT as a core direct mapping for value retail/private-label staples due to Walmart U.S. grocery scale, Great Value, Sam's Club, Member's Mark, and retail media/data monetization.
Add BJ as a focused warehouse-club/private-label candidate with Own Brands penetration and membership income metrics that are easier to isolate than Walmart or Costco.
Add TJX as the leading off-price chokepoint candidate where purchasing relationships and inventory turns may matter more than simple store count.
Add OLLI as a less obvious extreme-value/closeout retailer tied to excess-inventory sourcing and private-label supplementation.
Add UNFI as a second-order wholesale/private-label infrastructure candidate; thesis is weaker than direct retailers and requires margin, customer concentration, and owned-brand evidence.

Costco should be covered in a follow-up or leader pass: it is a core warehouse-club/private-label leader with Kirkland and high renewal economics, but omitted here to reserve slots for less obvious supplier/closeout mappings.

TreeHouse Foods would have been a high-quality private-label manufacturing pure play, but it completed a take-private transaction in February 2026 and should be tracked as private-market evidence rather than a current US-listed candidate.
Further pass should check DG, DLTR, BURL, ROST, KR, ACI, GO, CASY, SPTN, and grocery/private-label packaging or cold-chain suppliers for additional public-market mappings.

node: Value retail, clubs, off-price, dollar/value channels, and private-label staples
summary: Expanded universe focuses on retailers and second-order suppliers that can monetize consumer trade-down through purchasing scale, membership economics, private-label penetration, closeout sourcing, and grocery distribution leverage. The strongest direct mappings are Walmart/Sam's Club, BJ's Wholesale Club, TJX, and Ollie's; UNFI is included as a less obvious wholesale/private-label infrastructure candidate. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
